works.title: Tales from the Crypt
works.notes: Deep dive on the forgotten Tim Curry episode.

works.title: Beavis and Butt-Head
works.notes: Rights issues mean you can't stream a complete season anywhere.

works.title: Are You Afraid of the Dark?
works.notes: The show that kept a generation of kids up at night.

works.title: The Vampyre
works.notes: The 1819 novella that invented the modern aristocratic vampire.

works.title: Murder Party
works.notes: Micro-budget Brooklyn horror comedy made before Blue Ruin and Green Room.

works.title: The Dark Half
works.notes: Two horror legends, one forgotten film.

works.title: The Cricket in Times Square
works.notes: Belongs beside Charlotte's Web and Stuart Little. Six sequels almost nobody knows about.

works.title: Riverbend
works.notes: Red Dawn meets The Color Purple. Buried on VHS, rescued onto YouTube.

works.title: The Phantom Tollbooth
works.notes: Juster violated his Ford Foundation grant to write it.

works.title: Eerie, Indiana
works.notes: YA Twin Peaks shot on film. 19 episodes and gone.

works.title: Nightmare Seasons
works.notes: Four novellas, four seasons. Went head to head with King at the 1983 World Fantasy Awards.

works.title: Mimic
works.notes: The movie that almost ended del Toro's career. Watch the Director's Cut.

works.title: Mapping the Interior
works.notes: Bram Stoker Award winning novella most people skipped on the way to The Only Good Indians.

works.title: Savageland
works.notes: Found-photography horror. 57 people gone overnight and 37 photographs.

works.title: The Dark Descends
works.notes: Six Goodreads ratings. Collins Crime Club, same imprint as Agatha Christie.

works.title: Storm of the Century
works.notes: Give me what I want and I'll go away. Premiered Valentine's Day 1999.

works.title: Slumber Party
works.notes: The first book published under the Point imprint.

works.title: Near Dark
works.notes: Vampire Western buried by The Lost Boys. Forty night shoots, and three leads lifted from Aliens.

works.title: Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark
works.notes: The most banned book of the 1990s.

works.title: The Twilight Zone
works.notes: Serling came home from WWII with a Bronze Star, a Purple Heart, and something to say.

works.title: Flowers in the Attic
works.notes: 14 weeks on the NYT bestseller list. Nearly 100 books now carry her name.

works.title: I Am Legend
works.notes: Three adaptations across forty years. Every one of them missed the point.

works.title: The Garbage Pail Kids Movie
works.notes: Pulled from theaters after three weeks by organized protest.

works.title: Heat Vision and Jack
works.notes: The most expensive unaired pilot in network history. Survived on bootleg VHS.

works.title: Toy Cemetery
works.notes: Start of the killer toy quest. Great cover, abandons its own premise.

works.title: Dark Shadows
works.notes: Nearly 9 million daily viewers. Invented the sympathetic vampire.

works.title: House
works.notes: Dekker's 15 page treatment. A horror novelist relives Vietnam inside his aunt's house.

works.title: Absentia
works.notes: $23,000 on Kickstarter. He called it his last independent feature. He was right.

works.title: The Monster Squad
works.notes: Made back less than a third of its budget. Wolfman's got nards.

works.title: The Slumber Party Massacre
works.notes: The only American horror franchise where every entry is written and directed by women.

works.title: Keeper of the Children
works.notes: An axe-wielding stuffed bear and a climactic puppet battle. The quest continues.

works.title: The Faculty
works.notes: The Kevin Williamson script nobody mentions.

works.title: MaMa
works.notes: Five print runs, out of print for decades, brought back by her daughter.

works.title: The Ray Bradbury Theater
works.notes: Every episode adapted a Bradbury short story. Every screenplay written by Bradbury.

works.title: Prey
works.notes: The next stop on the killer toy quest. A Matheson short story about a Zuni fetish doll.

works.title: Blue Ruin
works.notes: The revenge thriller that put Saulnier on the map.

works.title: Green Room
works.notes: Saulnier’s punk-band siege film.

works.title: Charlotte's Web
works.notes: The children’s classic Cricket deserves to sit beside.

works.title: Stuart Little
works.notes: The other E. B. White animal classic everyone still remembers.

works.title: Red Dawn
works.notes: Half of the "Red Dawn meets The Color Purple" pitch for Riverbend.

works.title: The Color Purple
works.notes: The other half of the Riverbend comparison.

works.title: Twin Peaks
works.notes: Eerie, Indiana was described as YA Twin Peaks.

works.title: Different Seasons
works.notes: King’s four-novella collection that beat Nightmare Seasons at the 1983 World Fantasy Awards.

works.title: The Only Good Indians
works.notes: The breakout novel readers skipped Mapping the Interior to get to.

works.title: The Lost Boys
works.notes: Landed two months before Near Dark and buried it.

works.title: Aliens
works.notes: Near Dark pulled three of its leads straight from this cast.

works.title: Night of the Living Dead
works.notes: Romero named I Am Legend as his primary inspiration.

works.title: The Last Man on Earth
works.notes: The first I Am Legend adaptation.

works.title: The Omega Man
works.notes: The second I Am Legend adaptation.

works.title: I Am Legend (2007)
works.notes: The third adaptation, and the one that missed the ending hardest.

works.title: Maus
works.notes: The Pulitzer winner by the man who designed the Garbage Pail Kids cards.

works.title: Taxi Driver
works.notes: Scorsese gave Amy Holden Jones a PA gig here, which led to Corman.

works.title: Scream
works.notes: The Williamson script everyone mentions instead of The Faculty.

works.title: Trilogy of Terror
works.notes: The made-for-TV anthology whose final segment adapts Prey.

works.title: Tattooed Teenage Alien Fighters from Beverly Hills
works.notes: A 40-episode Power Rangers knockoff on the USA network that almost nobody remembers - rediscovered through a Dragon Ball Z Abridged joke. Cheap costumes, five sets, and writing far sharper than the kids' show it pretended to be.

works.title: Night of the Mannequins
works.notes: The next stop on the killer toy quest. A novella written in four days about a mannequin named Manny pulled out of a creek bed - and a slasher told entirely from the killer's point of view.

works.title: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers
works.notes: Saban's original, built by splicing licensed Japanese Super Sentai action footage with cheap American teen footage - the formula everyone else chased.

works.title: VR Troopers
works.notes: Saban's follow-up the next year, using a different Super Sentai series with the same formula.

works.title: Superhuman Samurai Cyber Squad
works.notes: DIC's first attempt at the formula, and the show that ran them out of licensable Japanese footage - which is why they shot Tattooed Teenage Alien Fighters entirely in America.

works.title: Big Bad Beetleborgs
works.notes: The recap Paris originally set out to do before this episode became a boondoggle.

works.title: Dragon Ball Z Abridged
works.notes: The fan redub whose gag list of martial arts shows made a generation discover Tattooed Teenage Alien Fighters was real.

works.title: Voltron
works.notes: Tommy raises it as the animated predecessor that spliced Japanese shows for an American audience; Paris calls it a contemporary of Power Rangers.

works.title: Beverly Hills 90210
works.notes: Paris keeps coming back to it: the show's real drama is teen interpersonal soap, with monster fights as window dressing.

works.title: The Room
works.notes: Fans of the Ameritoku genre call Tattooed Teenage Alien Fighters 'the Room of Ameritoku shows.'

works.title: On Writing
works.notes: Tommy invokes King's fossil metaphor - stories already exist and the writer excavates them - to describe how the novella found its own shape.

works.title: There Will Be Blood
works.notes: Paris's story about a moviegoer who felt cheated by the title - his analogy for the novella's negative reviews.
